newsitem.title: UK: Opinion polls put Labour on course to win election.
newsitem.headline: Opinion polls put Labour on course to win election.

text.p: The main opposition Labour Party is between 20 and 25 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives in the run-up to Britain's May 1 election, according to opinion polls published in Sunday newspapers.
An ICM poll for The Observer put Labour at 50 percent against 30 percent for the Conservatives and 14 percent for the minority centrist Liberal Democrats.
ICM carried out its poll between last Wednesday and Friday, before Labour leader Tony Blair suffered his first real setback of the campaign over plans for devolving power to Scotland.
An NOP poll for the Sunday Times gave Labour 52 percent, with the Conservatives at 28 percent and the Liberal Democrats 12 percent.
A MORI poll for the Sunday Mirror gave Labour 55 percent, the Conservatives 30 percent and the Liberal Democrats nine percent REUTER
